report:
## Conclusion

Based on the current body of evidence, **ivermectin does not appear to lower the risk of death from COVID-19.** Multiple large, well-conducted randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and updated meta-analyses have failed to demonstrate a mortality benefit.

### Key Evidence:

- **ACTIV-6 trial** (published in *JAMA*, October 2022): A large U.S. RCT found ivermectin was not effective as a COVID-19 treatment, showing no meaningful improvement in time to sustained recovery compared to placebo. ([JAMA](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2797483))

- **Higher-dose ivermectin trial** (published in *JAMA*, March 2023): Even at a higher dose (600 μg/kg for 6 days), ivermectin did not improve time to sustained recovery in mild-to-moderate COVID-19. The authors concluded: "These findings do not support the use of ivermectin." ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36807465/))

- **NEJM outpatient trial** (March 2022): Ivermectin did not reduce hospital admissions or prolonged emergency department observation among outpatients with early COVID-19. ([NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869))

- **Systematic review and meta-analysis** (BMC Infectious Diseases, July 2022): After accounting for retracted studies and evolving standards of care, the review found no conclusive evidence that ivermectin reduces mortality. A separate meta-analysis noted that while some earlier analyses suggested a mortality benefit, this was based on "low certainty of evidence" and was not confirmed by larger, higher-quality trials. ([Springer/BMC](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12879-022-07589-8))

### Regulatory Stance:
The **FDA has not approved ivermectin** for treating or preventing COVID-19, stating that available clinical trial data do not demonstrate effectiveness. The **Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA)** recommends against ivermectin for COVID-19 outpatients outside of clinical trials. ([FDA](https://www.fda.gov/search?s=ivermectin+for+covid))

### Summary:
While some early, smaller studies and preprints suggested a possible benefit, these were often methodologically flawed or later retracted. The totality of high-quality evidence from large RCTs and rigorous meta-analyses does not support that ivermectin reduces mortality in COVID-19.
